result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.hub_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get HITS hub scores for each node (directed graphs only). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19845-L19948){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.hub_centrality( max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} HITS (Hyperlink-Induced Topic Search) computes authority and hub scores for nodes in a directed graph. Hub score measures how much a node points to good authorities: `hub(v) = sum of authority scores of nodes v points to` Uses power iteration until convergence. Good hubs are nodes that point to many high-quality authorities. Requires a directed graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of iterations for convergence. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance threshold. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name for the node attribute to store results. If not provided, auto-generates name from method name (`hub_centrality`). [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary of results. If `False`, stores results as node attributes and returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to normalized hub scores. If `return_dict=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph is undirected. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Calculate hub scores in a citation network: ::: {#a3529ad1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="Paper1") .add_node(label="Paper2") .add_node(label="Paper3") .add_edge("Paper1", "Paper2") # Paper1 cites Paper2 .add_edge("Paper1", "Paper3") # Paper1 cites Paper3 ) graph.hub_centrality(return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: 1.0, 3: 0.0, 2: 0.0} ``` ::: ::: The roles are reversed from authority: "Paper1" scores highest here since it cites several other papers, while the cited papers score lowest. Store as node attributes and chain: ::: {#fc5e4779 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="Paper1") .add_node(label="Paper2") .add_node(label="Paper3") .add_edge(source="Paper1", target="Paper2") .add_edge(source="Paper1", target="Paper3") ) ( graph .hub_centrality(attr_name="hub") .rescale_node_attrs(node_attr_from="hub", node_attr_to="size") .describe() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Number of nodes : 3 Number of edges : 2 Directed : True Density : 0.33 Average degree (min, max) : 1.33 (1, 2) Strongly connected : False Weakly connected : True Number of strongly connected components : 3 Number of weakly connected components : 1 Computations on nodes: - hub_centrality() -> attr: 'hub' (3 of 3 nodes) Node aesthetics: - size <- hub via rescale (range: [0.5, 1.0]) (values: 0.5, 1.0, 3 of 3 nodes) ``` ::: :::
